evidence: src/infrastructure/http/SubscriptionController.ts: constructor injects StartSubscription, ChangeSeats and CancelSubscription from src/application/use-cases (application layer, which infrastructure may depend on)
create(body: StartBody) only calls this.start.execute(body.customerId, body.plan, body.seats)
resize(id, body: SeatsBody) only calls this.changeSeats.execute(id, body.seats)
cancel(id, body: CancelBody) awaits this.cancelSubscription.execute(id, body.reason) and returns the result, with no business decision
Candidate flag cohesion/low-cohesion (LCOM4 3): each handler uses a different injected use case, which is normal for a controller and doesn't put another layer's responsibility here
parsedVerdict.reasoning: SubscriptionController sits in the infrastructure (delivery) layer and does what that layer should do. It declares request body shapes (StartBody, SeatsBody, CancelBody). Its constructor injects application use cases, which is allowed wiring. Each handler maps fields from the request body to a use case's execute() call and returns the result. None of the handlers enforces an invariant, does a calculation or makes a business decision. The only extra statement is in cancel, which awaits the result and then returns it; that is not business logic. The low-cohesion flag (LCOM4 3) is accurate but doesn't break this rule. Each handler uses its own injected use case, which is normal for a thin controller and doesn't mean the class has another layer's role.
